And when did you start thinking about it? Well, I’ve always been interested in linguistics, but I'm also really interested in health and wellbeing from a policy perspective. Not sure if those mix well for a master’s but who knows. That's actually fascinating. Policy and health could make for a really impactful field, right? What draws you to it? I've always been interested in the way language impacts patient experience, and then also how we can translate that into tangible policy changes... really trying to make a difference from the grassroots up. But it's scary and overwhelming to think about starting a new program, especially when you're already juggling a full-time job. It’s scary, but also incredibly exciting, isn’t it? I mean, the potential career paths and personal fulfillment are huge draws. Have you thought about what’s holding you back besides just the time commitment? Honestly, it's a mix of fear of failure, fear of what others will think, but also just a feeling of being so comfortable in my current role that change feels daunting. Plus, it feels like a lot of commitment for something that might not work out. I feel you. But I mean, isn’t fear of not trying even greater? And who cares what others think as long as it makes you happy? That's the thing...

So tell me about your week, did you manage to get any's plant shopping done? Yeah I did actually. I ended up going to the Milton Nursery. Got some garlic chives, they're supposed to be really good for keeping the mosquitos away. Ah right, I'd heard that about the chives. But garlic and onions, they're a part of my plant arsenal too. I've got this big tub of mint that I use to keep the slugs away and it's also good for making tea keeps it fresh. You're really into your gardening, aren't you? It's amazing to see your indoor plants thriving. I've been meaning to ask - did your avacado plant actually come to any fruition? LOL, well actually yes - after making sure the soil and climate were properly checked and all that. It's been about two years now and it started bearing fruit, but only one or two avocados per year. But it's still such a rewarding thing. You couldn't buy that kind of taste anywhere. That's brilliant, it's like having a miniature garden in the kitchen. I've been trying to grow a lemongrass plant from the supermarket, but it just doesn't seem keen. Oh they can be tricky, but you can give it more light, really make sure it's at a warm spot or even near a window that gets loads of indirect sunlight. And perhaps mist it a bit, they like humid air. Yeah I've tried that, but I think the key might be getting the right amount of water. I always end up overwatering and things start to rot. Exactly - plants are like children, you have to give them attention and make sure they're not the ones making all the decisions. More often than not, underwatering is better, they're more susceptible to that than overwatering. That's solid advice. It reminds me of my aunt, she always said "if in doubt, leave it alone - the natural environment usually takes care of itself." I like that, that's some good plant wisdom. Speaking of wisdom, I made a rhubarb tart this week - so good. Reminds me of my gran's recipes. You know, I've been meaning to try baking. There's something almost therapeutic about it, just being in the moment with the dough and all.

Ah, Phil, did you manage any gardening this weekend or was it just football gods today? Yeah, I managed a bit. Had to tidy up before the predicted storms and of course, watering all the new seedlings. You know, the weather now, it's either a barbecue weekend or questions if we're just one hose-width away from desertification. Hose-width away indeed. I'm still struggling with why my pride fractals never seem to fill themselves up like Morphy. Right, let me not get started on my succulents, okay? But I did see a very engaging documentary on grasses that had survived millennia despite mankind's best efforts. Sentimental, just like my football. Ah, speaking of surviving efforts, did you see that article about old players' kids making a bit of a fuss in the media? Looks like they're either mini-commentators or just looking for a slice of fame too. Yes, I did. It's a weird thing, isn't it? I mean, I hope they find whatever path they're interested in, but the youth cult and celebrity culture - it's a whole different world from what we knew. Indeed. Speaking of another 'world', did you see the new snooker lineup? Any favorites emerging? Ah, snooker, yes. I had a look. There's always some new talent coming through, but, you know, the old guard can still surprise us all. I'm rooting for Ronnie still, but I'm also intrigued by the young ones - they bring a fresh style, but sometimes it's like they're playing a different game altogether. Ronnie's still got it, I reckon. I just wish they'd have more matches less dependent on the TV's technical preferences. Snooker's more visual than most sports, you'd think they'd prioritize getting the skills on screen rather than just making it look flashy. Exactly. I've also been marking some work from our new students. Some of them are showing real promise, but I'm also noticing a few habits we need to work on. You know, it's not just about knowing the facts, it's how to articulate them properly too. Right. That's where experience comes in. Some of these new recruits almost make you wish for the old days where maybe technique wasn't everything but knowledge and understanding were prioritized. Well, I've seen officers come and go, each with their different views on how to apply the law and book knowledge to real situations.

So have you thought about what you're gonna do for your birthday questions again this year? Yeah I've got a few ideas floating about, but I'll need to figure out the logistics and make sure it actually fits into our schedule. Can we have a water park day again? Oh honey, I don't think Daddy has enough money for a water park day this year. But we can plan something fun at home or in your garden. Maybe we can even have a little party with your friends if we can figure out a good date. Yeah, and then for Christening plans, have you made a decision on when/where it's going to be yet? We're thinking maybe in the summer when it's a bit warmer and hopefully we can invite more family. The church service would happen in the morning and then a little gathering at home in the afternoon. We're trying to keep it quite intimate but still special for all of us. Can we have a cake though, with lots of sprinkles? Of course, we'll make sure to have a nice cake with lots of sprinkles. Maybe even a little themed one if you'd like. Speaking of plans, how's work been? You've been fairly quiet about it. It's all good, thanks for asking. Just the usual ups and downs but doesn't feel too overwhelming at the moment. Just trying to keep on top of everything. And you're still thinking of changing jobs in the next year? More like hoping. The field I'm in, it's a bit tough right now. But I'm doing my best to prepare for when the right opportunity comes along. I want to play! Can we play now? Not right now, sweetie, but after we finish talking for a bit. Maybe we can play a game together or you can go play in your room with your toys. What do you think? So, this Christening... have you thought about asking certain family members to be involved? I know it's traditional for some but I'm not sure if we want to go that route. I've been thinking about it but I'm a bit torn too. Traditional or not, it's a big decision. We'll likely go with something simpler and less formal if we can.

Oh the tea is ready isn't it. Want a cup?      Yes please, thanks! You've always been the best at making it so quick!      Can I have some too?      Now, shall I start with your tea or wait until everyone is here?      Think it's probably best to get started before we start getting everyone's different orders.      Mmm, makes sense to me. Okay, just like you like it then.      Thank you so much!      Can I have some honey?      Of course, sweetheart.           So, I've been thinking about the plans for New York. Have you guys talked at all or wanted to start planning any specific activities yet?      Can we see the Statue of Liberty?      I think so, yes. We should definitely put that on the list. Any other things we should consider or are there certain places you all have always wanted to visit?      I was thinking Central Park, maybe some good food spots... and we should book tickets for a Broadway show, considering we’re probably going to be there on a weekend and they usually have a lot of popular ones going on.      And can we go to the Children's Museum?      Definitely. I'll definitely look into those. We weren't sure, were we, about when exactly it would be suitable to go? If it fits in couple of months' time?      Yeah, exactly. While the weather is changing, we should try to go before it gets really hot or too cold.      Can I go in the winter too? I want snow in New York!      Maybe for the next one, sweetheart. But this time, let's see the city in a more comfortable climate.      We can always do another adventure when it's winter, right?      Exactly. Now, moving on to plans for the weekend here. Have you thought of anything specific for tomorrow or Sunday?      We could have a picnic... maybe outside if the weather is nice.      That sounds lovely! Although, I was also planning to tidy up a bit in the garden if it doesn't rain tomorrow afternoon.      Brilliant combination—a bit of gardening with the promise of a picnic afterwards.      And as soon as everyone is a bit more settled, we can start going through what we need to do for the holiday, right?      Absolutely. And I've been meaning to look up some of those Broadway ticket options.      Can we take my baby doll?

So okay so I had this thing for educ maths first year's assessment. Oh, okay. Right, and they wanted us to complete these booklets on various concepts. I remember that now, the old booklets with all the pages on questions. Yes, and one of them got me. Like this question on "Pascals' Triangle and Binomial Expansion". I had trouble with that too. Always found it a bit tricky to keeps changing those coefficients alongside the numbers in the triangle. Exactly. Like how do you prove that the sum of the numbers in each row equals to that perfect square? Oh, is that what you're looking at here? Yeah, that whole "proof by induction" part. Yeah, induction is a bit hard to grasp at first. I know, right? But when you finally get it, it feels so good. It's those "aha" moments, especially in maths. So what did you do about it? So, I went over my lecture notes, and then I watched some videos on YouTube. Yeah, the university puts its lectures online sometimes, but sometimes you can't find the perfect explanation. Exactly. So I found this one guy, Alex, who has this channel where he does in-depth explanations of really hard concepts. Ah, you mean that 'The Mathematics Guy' channel? Yeah! That's the one. He explained it so simply, like finding the fifth row and then proving that each time you're adding integers together the sum will always be a perfect square. Oh right, I always struggle with base case foundations in proofs by induction. Yeah, but getting that first step right, really helps. So then you can easily see how to build the rest. Makes sense. So I spent a few hours with that. Then for the assignment, I made sure I outlined my proof clearly. That's good because when you're explaining an abstract concept like that in writing, it has to be clear. Exactly. I ended up doing a flowchart to show each step I was proving and that came in handy for the examples too. Flowcharts are a lifesaver. I've started doing those more and more in my essays. Definitely. And I also made sure to relate it back to the first principles. Like connecting it to the basic idea of why Pascals’ Triangle is used in the first place? Yes, connecting it back to combinatorics and why integer sums in that particular arrangement behave that way.

So okay let's talk about what we could buy if we won the Lottery. Assuming the Lottery prizes are still worth something after the cost of a dog. Mommy, can we get a dog? Yeah, a dog! So, if we could afford anything, what would it be? A big house, a fancy car? But actually, I've always dreamed of opening a little local café. Serve homemade cakes and keepsakes for kids. Think about it, our own little spot where everyone knows everyone, and kids can run around. Like the one by the park? Yes, that kind of thing. That's actually really nice. And then we can have the kids helping out, little jobs to teach them responsibility. And I can help make cupcakes for the café! Definitely, you would be the main baker. And it would be a place where families can come together. Yeah! And we could have a little play area too, with blocks and stuff. I can see it. And we could have special dog-friendly days for those with well-behaved dogs. Exactly. A safe place for families and their dogs. And can we take Emmy? She's really good. Sure, if she's trained to behave around others, we could have a pet area. That's quite a dream. How about helping out with chores at home to practice the skills we'd need? I can help with setting the table! And I can help clean up! And, if we matched numbers in the Lottery and won a decent amount, we could use some of that to educate ourselves on running a business, or maybe even take some business courses. You know, it's interesting to think about. I've always just thought of a dog, somewhere comfortable for them to run. But now, I like the idea of it being more intertwined with our daily lives. Can we dream about a dog? Again and again! Alright, let's dream harder. What kind of dog do you both want? A fluffy one. A funny one. And something that won't mind spending time at the café, like maybe this really cool dog breed... Do you know, the Lottery isn't just about material things. It could bring us closer together, maybe give us the freedom to pursue what truly makes us happy as a family, like opening that café, or spending more time outside with a dog.

So, you had to go to A&E this past weekend? Yeah, the mountain bike accident was kind of a freak incident. I just lost control near the end of the trail and hit a tree. Oh no, I'm glad you're okay, that sounds really serious. What happened? Did you break anything? I'm mostly banged up - bruises and scrapes everywhere. But I did end up with a concussion. They kept me overnight at the hospital, did a scan to make sure it wasn't anything too serious. That's frightening. Do you remember anything about the accident itself? Yeah, the last thing I remember properly was trying to avoid a certain turn, and then the next thing I knew, I was on the ground, looking up at some branches. I must have blacked out for a bit because I couldn't remember getting there. Someone who was running behind me heard the crash or saw me fall and came to help. They called an ambulance on the spot. That’s really lucky. Did they advise anything specific for recovery? Yeah, the doc just told me to rest as much as I can for the next week or two and keep an eye on any symptoms for concussion - headache worse than normal or persistent, dizziness, sensitivity to light, things like that. They also gave me a note about maybe taking some time off from work until I get a green light from my own doc. That doesn’t sound ideal but clearly it’s the sensible thing to do. Are you planning on getting back on that mountain bike anytime soon? Honestly, I'm not sure just yet. I think I’ll take a bit more caution for a while. I was actually pretty confident with it, so it was a bit of a blow to see how quickly things can go wrong. Definitely a perspective changing moment. Accidents are scary especially when we think we’re in control. Exactly. It makes you appreciate health and safety and all those protocols we often roll our eyes at. Yeah, and maybe review some of your safety gear? That’s actually top of my list once this is over. I guess the real job will be trying to figure out what I did wrong and if there’s anything I can improve for next time. Always a good idea to learn from each experience.

You heard the news about the new immigration policy from the government? Yes, I heard about it. It seems like another complicated issue. Do you think it will affect your business in any way? Well, I hope not. But honestly, with all the changes happening, it's hard to predict. I've always tried to support local talent, but sometimes it's just not enough. What about your shop? You're dealing with customers from all over, right? Yeah, it's a bit like that. But you know, Hove's always been a place where people from all over can feel welcome. Of course, that might change with new policies. But I think the real challenge is the economic uncertainty - people aren't looking for splurge purchases right now. They're holding on to their money tightly. True. It's like every business owner I talk to is feeling the pinch. I recently had a meeting with some of the other business leaders in the area. We're all trying to brainstorm ways to adapt. I'm seriously considering moving some of my activities online. What about you? Any new ideas on the horizon? Actually, yes. I've been thinking of expanding our delivery service. If people are spending more time at home, perhaps they'd love to have our tea and coffee delivered right to their doorstep? Plus, with all the new health-focused trends, I'm thinking about offering a 'wellness tea' selection. Just been looking at some interesting herbal blends from the distributors I work with. That could work. People are indeed prioritizing health more these days. But the logistics of delivery could be tricky, especially if it’s tea that needs to be handled carefully. I've heard it can be quite a challenge getting things delivered fresh and hot. Absolutely, but I’ve spoken to some friends who run delivery services and they’ve been advising on proper packaging and timings. Plus, if we market it right – emphasizing that it’s for ‘comfort in these uncertain times’ – it might just hit the spot. I like the sound of that. ‘Comfort in uncertain times’ is a brilliant tagline. Plus, the environmental angle. Less people driving out for a café visit, lower carbon footprint... You could really market that as part of your brand's commitment to sustainability. Exactly! I was thinking to pair it with a social media campaign that encourages people to enjoy their tea outdoors – finding that small bit of peace and quiet...

Still up for trying the new pub menu tonight then? Oh definitely! I've heard great things about the pub and I'm looking forward to trying them out. Me too, right? Although I've been thinking, we should also pick up some snacks from that new shop near the station. It's got a few unique items that might complement our meal nicely. That sounds like a plan. By the way, have you seen the new season of Happy Valley? I was just binge-watching it over the weekend. No, but from what I've heard, it's just as well-done as the previous seasons. I'll definitely catch up soon. Worth a try for sure. The character development and storytelling in that show are spot on. And it explores such complex themes. Someone should study the appeal of mysteries and justice or lack thereof in British television. Maybe I can use some of that show as examples for my upcoming university assignment. That's a great idea. I assumed you'd already finished everything. Good luck with the assignment; it sounds quite interesting. Thanks, but I do have an interesting topic. Anyway, speaking of interesting things, have you noticed the décor in here? It's all so nostalgic isn't it? Old photographs of Woolwich and everything. Yeah, they've done a great job with it. I like how they’ve incorporated local history into the atmosphere. Makes me feel like we're kind of holding onto the past, while also enjoying the present. Exactly. Though, have you seen my coat? It’s still a bit wet, blurred out the whole base. I should have left it to dry properly. Oh, did you dry it yesterday? I could lend you a hair dryer if you need to speed the process up. No, no, it's fine. Just need to let it dry for a bit longer. Right. Also, have you listened to that new band on the radio? It's real catchy. I have, the music is quite quirky but in a good way. Wonder if any of our music lessons with Martin from university would help us analyze that better. Oh Martin. Always criticizing our choices but secretly influencing our tastes. I know! He was quite particular about... The order of classical pieces? Or if you didn't play a scale perfectly? Yeah, exactly. Martin and his scales.

So how are you enjoying that new camera? It's been great! I've been taking some shots around Edinburgh. There's so much to capture. Still trying to get the hang of all the manual settings though. Oh don’t worry, it gets easier with practice. I remember getting out into the countryside and just experimenting. The best lessons you learn right there, in the field I'd say! Yeah, exactly that! I've been meaning to get out to Fife. You know, before we had that rainy spell. Right, the weather had been quite unpredictable, hasn't it? I almost gave up any thought of taking my camera out. But as you say, there’s beauty in the rain, if you can capture it right. Definitely. I’ve actually taken some interesting shots during storms. The light changes so much. But sometimes it can be a bit tricky, you know, keeping the lens dry and all. Absolutely, I’ve had my fair share of floods on camera trips! For me, it’s usually about waiting and watching for moments when the rain is less heavy. Or when the sun just starts to peep through. That can provide some really dramatic shots. Yeah, that’s true, there’s always a window. And people carrying umbrellas or sitting in alleyways can add some really human elements to the photo, especially if you’re doing street photography in bad weather. Street photography is always so much about timing and observation. You learn to anticipate when someone’s about to look up or step into that beam of light breaking through the clouds. Or like, you know, the reflections off wet pavement during the rain. Edinburgh’s streets can be so dull under normal light, but just throw some rain on it and suddenly you’ve got shinier cobblestones and interesting reflections everywhere. Absolutely! And the mood and atmosphere you can capture with rain or mist changing the whole feel of a scene. You end up with these sort of moody, introspective shots that you wouldn’t get on a bright sunny day. Yeah! And it’s so much about timing. I took a shot of the statue of David Hume on a wet afternoon, and the mist was rolling off the North Sea, and it was this melancholic scene. Maybe I’ll post that up on my socials later if you’re interested.

So, what's on for this week? You got the usual nursery runtimes or are they changing anything this term? Ah, yes they moved one of the sessions and now I've got a bit of a gap between dropping them off and starting work. I might have to squeeze in some prep work at home I suppose. Oh, that's a bit awkward isn't it? Think about working something in at home. Yeah, I thought I could use the mornings for that since they'll be busy at nursery. Plus, I've got that new online course to work through. I'm looking to get a better understanding of digital literacy in the classroom - oh, and how I can apply it properly with my class. That sounds like a sensible plan. Do you know what, I'm a little bit nervous about juggling everything - it seems like there's so much to do these days as a teacher, or as a mother! But the course looks really interesting. I've been there, believe me. These busy periods are just part of it now and then, but the course will be useful. If it helps with the kids' education, that's great, right? Absolutely, and technology is such a big part of their current lives even at that young age. Hopefully, it'll enrich my lessons and in turn help the children. But you never know, sometimes the tech and all the accreditation stuff and "proper teaching methods" can feel a bit overwhelming. There you go - the 'rat race' of education. I don't envy you having to do all the extra bits. Seems like the profession's got a whole lot more paperwork and expectations. It does feel that way. Anyway, another thing - did you hear about the playdate this weekend for Annabelle? There will be another baby there so I'm hoping the older ones will help take care of themselves a little. Ah yes, that sounds like fun - or chaos depending on how it goes! At least it's a structure for you so you can run some errands or relax a bit. Exactly, and maybe I'll get some baking done. That always feels like a relaxing activity to me. Maybe I'll even put the course material down and watch some daytime TV! TV is fine sometimes. Just get something on that doesn't require continuous attention.

So have you heard the new team lead is kind of a nightmare, right? Yeah, I'd heard rumors. But have you actually dealt with them yet? Not yet, but... I had a bit of a disagreement with them at the last project review. Oh no. What happened? Well, we were discussing the timeline for the marketing event, and they were pushing for something that just wasn’t feasible. It just felt like they didn’t understand what we’re capable of given the resources we have. Yeah, that does sound frustrating. It’s like they’re disconnected from the actual work we do. Exactly. I’m hoping it might get better over time, but until then, we’re going to have to make sure to communicate expectations really clearly. Perhaps we need a bit of a rethink on how we handle our team lead and make sure our concerns are being heard. --- Speaking of difficult situations, I had a rather awkward moment with one of my clients the other day. Oh really? What happened? Well, we had a meeting to discuss the new project, and I made, let’s say, an... error in suggesting a fairly impractical solution based on a miscommunication about their budget. Oh no, I can imagine how that went down. But it’s good you realized the mistake and were able to correct it, right? Yes, thankfully, the client was understanding and we were able to adjust together. But it did make me realize the importance of double-checking details before meetings whenever possible. --- Changing topics, but have you seen those new boots in the window at  That Boutique  on King’s Street? No, I haven’t had a chance to check that out yet. I’m in a bit of a clothing rut currently, to be honest. I might go check them out soon. They’ve got some nice pieces coming in, and it’s about time I treated myself to something new. Maybe meet up next weekend and go shopping together. I could use some new stuff too. That sounds like a plan. We could get something to eat afterward, maybe something at Robinson’s or something similar. --- And while we’re making plans, I’ve been thinking... maybe it’s time we also planned a DIY project? A DIY project? What kind of project? Well, I’ve been wanting to spruce up my living room with some new wall decorations and thought it could be fun to do with you two.

Right, now I'm going to make some tea. Anyone want's any? Yes please, what's yours like today? It's just a strong tea with two sugars. I'll have that too. You know I prefer mine black, no sugar. Right, one black tea and two strong teas coming up. Have you tried out that new teapot I got? Erm, no I haven’t. You should get a look at it its pretty neat, has this ceramic infuser. Yeah I’ve always had a bit of a thing for fancy teaware. Is that the one with the little elephants on it? Exactly! Yeah, it’s quite the conversation piece. I’ll stick to what I know. Now let me check if we’ve got some Earl Grey too. That would be lovely actually, Earl Grey please. Right then, Earl Grey for you. We’ve got a bit of a rummage so let this serve as a moment to see if we're fully stocked up. These busybody retirements never seem to leave room for shopping while the kids were at home. It’s interesting how we all enjoy tea in our own way. I used to have it with milk and two sugars like you, but after I started my childminding days, I switched to black as a quick in between. I had no choice but to switch to black as well when I became a teacher. First thing in the morning and during breaks was all it was. Still is the case now, really. You both jumped into the profession fairly young. I stayed in the same career for three decades. More a settled routine, less of the caffeinated sprints. Different times for all of us, but tea remained constant. While you were slogging through a lifetime changing the world byte by byte, I was changing nappies and dealing with 3 a.m. wake-ups. Can’t say I miss any of it but it had its moments. Reminds me of my times though—full of sweet little faces and cries for more biscuits. Now it’s just a quiet house and the occasional job I take on to keep myself out of mischief. And the tea keeps us going. Always something to look forward to, especially when it's made well. Someone’s got a bit of a knack for it this mornings. Thanks! Just don’t take that as the norm, I was a bit short on time.

So tell me about that pub you mentioned yesterday. Oh yeah, it's The Red Lion. They've got this amazing new chef, he's been talked about all over the county. The food is not just pub grub. Aye and the atmosphere is great. Friendly staff, nice views over the countryside. I've heard they even have a decent selection of ales, not just the usual lagers and bitters. That sounds lovely. We should plan a trip there for my next visit out East. Definitely. You'll need it to relax, especially after all the stress with the new CRB checks at work. CRB checks?! Are they really that involved now? They're much stricter than in the past. I've even had to do a session on safeguarding this week. Does it apply to every job that involves working with people? Pretty much. Firefighters, teachers, anyone working with children or vulnerable adults. It's to make sure everyone's safe. That's wise. So what's this about a protest in London you were mentioning? Oh yes, I saw a message from some friends who were involved. It was about the new driving laws and how they discriminate against certain groups. Yeah, apparently the amendments were rushed through and they're facing a lot of backlash for not considering all perspectives. Politics is always a can of worms, isn’t it? Well, there's art too, right? I went to see that new exhibit at the Tate Modern, it was fascinating. Very true. There's always art to escape into, if one needs it. Indeed. Speaking of escape, do any of you know good, affordable hotels in London? I might be needing one soon. There's The Hoxton in Shoreditch. It's quite trendy but great value, and changing the scenery can help refresh one’s mind. And it's a bit more laid-back than the City. Plus, for a drink, it's just nearby. Reminds me, we should have a family trip to London soon. Maybe show little Sophie the Changing of the Guard? That sounds like a plan. And perhaps meet up with Speaker_4 in London. I haven’t seen you guys in ages. Definitely. And maybe we can all meet up for dinner at that pub Speaker_2 mentioned. The Red Lion? That would be... perfect. Speaking of dinner, this was excellent, wasn’t it? Yes, and I’m very grateful for the amazing spread.

Hey, did I miss anything?? We've been away for nearly two weeks and I'm super excited to catch up. Oh hey! Are you still here? Hi! Sorry to freak you out, but yes, you did miss – well, questions about the kitchen situation and conversations about work and house hunting. Kitchen situation? Yeah. The fridge's broken down and it's affecting our food planning until it gets fixed. Also, guess who's coming over for game night this weekend? Game night? Who’s visiting? The usual gang plus your ex. Might have been premature to share that but. Ah, really? What’s the plan with that? Just a friendly game night, mate. The living room’s going to be full. Ron also said he’s thinking of moving apartments soon, so he might want some advice on trusted letting agents or somethin’. Ron’s searching for a new place already? Yeah. He thinks he found something nice but needs to know if it has any dodgy history. I might have to give him the lowdown in good time. Do we also need to prepare anything for the game night? Honestly? We just need snacks and good vibes. And in your case, possibly an open mind about certain exes being in the same room. Fair enough. Okay, I'll start mentally preparing myself for that. You’ll be fine, and if it’s any consolation, Jess will join too – the More Carefree Jess, so a few level-heads are coming along for good measure. Ah, okay. Good to know. How’s work been since I left? Work’s been changing a bit. With my new role, we might be facing some… restructuring, though that’s more talk than action for now. Our team loves our current set-up, but you can't always take things for granted. So, how’s everyone else in the family? Everyone’s good, thanks for asking. Mum got a new garden plan going; wanting to extend into our back yard, so that’ll be fun to see progress on. That’s great, she loves hobbies. Have you seen any of that recently? Speaker_1 and Speaker_2 : Now listen, let's talk about this tax thing they've been talking about. It's not as simple as they make it out to be. What particular policy? The one about tax cuts for businesses. They say it's to help the economy grow, but I'm not convinced it's going to help everyone. Why not? More money for businesses should mean more jobs, shouldn't it? Generally, that's the plan. However, in practice, it's not always that straightforward. You see, when businesses see a tax cut, they often just keep the money for themselves or use it to increase bonuses for their top executives, not to hire new people. But can't the government enforce something like that? Make sure the money goes to new hires and benefits? Sure, they could do more oversight, but that sometimes gets complicated. Politicians often want to keep things simple so the voters can understand it. And it's often about showing support for businesses, seen as key to economic growth. For me, it seems like it should be about making sure everyone benefits, not just the already wealthy. Exactly my point. It's about where the priorities lie. This government seems more focused on supporting businesses to increase profits, rather than ensuring the average person sees an actual improvement in their living standards. Like, what about people who work, but still can't afford a decent place to live? They talk about "trickle-down economics". The idea is that if you give money to the top, they'll create jobs, and the benefits will "trickle down" to everyone else. But the reality is far from that simple. We've seen it before; the gap between rich and poor just keeps getting wider. So, what could be done differently? Well, another approach could be to invest more in public services, creating jobs in healthcare, education, and infrastructure. Not only does this directly provide jobs, but it also improves the standard of living for everyone by ensuring better access to essential services. Plus, these kinds of investments can stimulate local economies more directly because the spending happens locally, unlike corporate investments which might just go overseas or into bank accounts. So, the tax policy could be used to fund those kinds of investments instead? Ideally, yes. We could also look into more progressive taxation, where those who have more pay a bit more to help fund these public investments.

Yeah's things have changed so much. When I was young, folk would talk about Labour and Conservatives, and talked about whether the country should have a mayor or not. It was simple, really. So, what did your friends think of having a mayor then? Mostly they thought it was unnecessary and a waste of money. And to an extent, they were right. It’s all about who you vote for, isn’t it? It’s not like the mayor makes such a big difference in day-to-day life, except possibly for those living in the city centres. But the perception was that it would shift power away from council members or even Parliament. That makes sense. So, they didn’t like it. Not really. But funnily enough, the biggest controversy then wasn’t about the mayor; it was about the council voting to close the old library and open a new one by the shopping centre. Some thought it was progress while others saw it as eroding culture. Libraries are so important. I wish we had more of them here, or at least the old one was still open. I know what you mean. But that's where the new technologies and the internet come in, right? It’s not just books nowadays. I don’t understand it all myself, but the future is less about physical libraries and more about being able to access information wherever, whenever. But sometimes I just want to hold a book or read one in a quiet room without my phone buzzing every other minute! I understand that completely. There's value in the tactile experience. Maybe that's one of those things that will make a comeback in the years to come, for those who appreciate it. Either way, it’s about balance, I suppose. Gran, what about the parties themselves? Like the Labour and the Conservatives? Are those still around? Oh, they’re still around! You’ve got Labour, and Conservatives, and Lib Dems. But the landscape has changed. New parties have emerged, like UKIP earlier, which shook things up but then sorta fizzled out after the Brexit vote.

So, speaking of family meals, did I ever tell you about the time during Grace's school summer feast? No, what happened? It’s a lovely spot and it’s been a while since the family's gone on a big outing there.

We've done some work on the impact of Arabic loanwords in English, particularly in terms of science and math, which of course comes from a time when Arabic was a hub of knowledge.      It's quite interesting, really, and it makes you wonder about the entire language changing trajectory if certain historical events had unfolded differently.      True. I spent some time living in the Mediterranean during my research years, and it's astonishing when you hear how much influence Arabic has had on the local languages, like Andalusian Spanish and various Mediterranean dialects.      That must've been an incredible experience. I've always wanted to travel there and experience the language in its regional context. I started learning Chinese recently, and it's opened a whole new world of linguistic and cultural connections.      Oh, Chinese! You know, the typology of that language is so different from anything... I mean, any European language, for sure.

Speaker_1 and Speaker_2 :   So, you've likely heard a lot about this coming referendum in Scotland, right?     Yeah, I've read about it quite a bit. It's about whether Scotland stays in the UK or becomes independent.     Spot on. Do you think you understand why some Scots might want to leave?     Well, I've got a keepsake here from a trip. It's a pin from my school trip to Edinburgh, and it says "Visit Scotland — Explore our outstanding history, diverse culture, and breathtaking landscapes." Seems like they've got a strong cultural identity to draw on. But I guess beyond that, some might feel that political decisions made in London don't always reflect Scottish interests. And there’s also the hydrocarbon wealth in the North Sea which they might feel they should control more directly.     Exactly. The debate centers around these things — self-governance and economic control. Some also argue for the potential benefits of making all decisions or even just some key ones that directly affect Scotland more locally. Whereas, the 'Better Together' side is about the economic and political benefits of being part of a larger union.     Right. I mean, think of it like our school council sometimes. If you don’t like how the school is run or you feel decisions are made without considering all students’ interests, you might want more say, right? But is it worth it in practice? Would Scotland be okay economically? They’re talking about keeping the pound, but would that work?     That’s a good example. But it’s not just about the pound. There’s the issue of EU membership, defense, and so on. Some say Scotland might face higher economic risks or less influence on the world stage without being part of a larger entity, while others argue that as a small independent nation, they could gain more direct advantages in various global forums by acting independently.     There’s also talk of national identity, feeling proud to be Scottish and not English or British. Is that a big factor do you think?     Identity sure plays a role. For some, it’s about being able to take pride in being Scottish without having to be part of a broader British identity. It's not necessarily about separating from the UK culturally but about political and economic autonomy. However, others might feel just as deeply British and see Scotland as an integral part of that.

Oh, did you hear that?? "Should've have gone to school more!" That's the kind of advice you'd expect to hear on Jeremy Kyle. What did you expect, educational strategies? Like, they're missing out verbal elisions and stuff, it's just 'could of' instead of 'could have', 'should of' instead of 'should have'. You'd think people on TV would at least get the grammar right. But no, changing the channel and learning something new on YouTube might be a better use of our time. I mean, in a way, it’s sad because those are real people, but also so much of it is staged for effect. It does real damage to the image of education and literacy in the public eye. Speaking of which, anyone else notice in the wider British media, how accents are sometimes used for laughs or to stereotype? Like certain dialects automatically make you sound less intelligent. For sure. It's all so frustrating because there's a huge amount of variation in how people speak English across the country, and most of it is just about where you're from.

Did you see that article in The Guardian about sleep? They have some funky neighborhoods over there, and all of a sudden, you're in the middle of a hipster community with good food everywhere. Oh, that sounds like fun. Do you ever get to fly? But you know, I often fly into Heathrow when I go back home. And there’s this one pilot who always seems to land the plane so smoothly. Yeah, I agree with skilled pilots making a big difference. Once, I watched this YouTuber who specializes in analyzing commercial flights for pilot technique.

So, you've really got to handle the hamster, the right way. If you do, they’ll be as kind as ginger cats . Speaker_2 : Ah, ginger cats, right? My sister has one. So, friendly? And maybe someday I’ll have a hamster and a ginger cat, and they’ll just show us what individuality is. That sounds like the perfect idea. And seriously, who knew there could be so much to talk about when it comes to pets and...gorgeous people with ginger hair? Well, I guess that’s what happens when you get a group of friends together from different parts of England.

Speaker_1's Mother's house in Bedford   Speaker Relationships: Speaker_1 and Speaker_2 are brothers and Speaker_3 is their mother   Activity: They're playing a game of Risk   Conversation Type: Discussing Risk strategies, joking around, making life comments, and reminiscing --- "Someone needs to take out Australia. We've been too lenient on the continent." "Only if we're sure this isn't Australia's year, mum. Remember, in '96, we nearly lost the whole game to this 'plush and quite frankly problematic' island nation." "True, true. Where did you get that from? '96? You're giving away your age with these references." "Well, it was my first year without you two, so I had to take over the game showmanship." "Assuming your 'showmanship' wasn't just a result of being 10 years old and easily distracted?" "Okay, I concede that point. But now, how about this 'Genghis Khan'-like strategy with Russia and Asia?" "Uh, let's not try to conquer the world just yet, shall we? The last time we took on that kind of risk, we had to call it a night before bedtime rolled around." "Remember when changing the board to a map of our local area was the 'generous' offer to avoid a full-scale world war for the night?" "Yeah, because nothing says 'cool evening activity' like mixing 'Risk' with a complicated land map of Bedford and surroundings. 'And this blue bit here is the river, kids. Don't turn it into a sea just yet...'" "I still think if we played that version with actual chocolate as currency, the game could've been saved. We'd all be so distracted by the chocolate that no one would mind who took over what." "Given some of our past strategies, maybe the chocolate distraction would've actually made you both more strategic. 'I'll trade you a carrot for a piece of this delicious chocolate bar' leading to a series of unexpected alliances." "Alright, new rule for future games: no eating the game pieces unless you've successful invaded Enfield. That's how we roll—or should I say, no, we don't roll, we conquer." "Speaking of Enfield, have you ever noticed how people pronounce it? It's 'En-field', not 'Nef-feld'. It's a common mistake, but it always bugs me." "Right. It's like when people mispronounce 'Bedford' as 'Bed-ford' instead of 'Bed-fud'.

Oh, Lena, I don't know if I have enough time today to fill these out. You're always chicken when it comes down to career plans. Chickening out now, aren't you? I'm just kind of... overthinking and underfeeling, and I'm sure you've been there! We've all been there, Lou. All of it. The hopes and fears of keeps coming backwards and forwards, like a carousel. Yeah, and now I'm questioning if I should have applied for more universities, just in case. I just have this feeling that whatever I pick, it just won't fit. But isn't that just part of the process? None of us really know what we’re doing until we're kind of already doing it, right? I mean, I thought I'd be a history major, and now I'm in English with a minor in sociology. And last year, I thought I'd never touch biology again, and now I love it! So, plans are... flexible. Planning is like trying to glue different puzzle pieces together with silly putty. The pieces keep shifting while the glue doesn't stick. Exactly! What if I do whatever and then become unemployed? A university dropout turned, like, 'At Least I Tried: The Documentary Series.' Oh, Lou, you're daft. We're talking real worries here. No, but serious, we've been all thinking if what we're doing now is really career stuff or just the stepping stones we think we’re supposed to take, right? Right. I mean, everyone's chasing job security but nobody knows what job security looks like next year, let alone five years from now. And then add onto that the societal pressure of 'having a plan' or becoming a 'successful person.' I don't know, it’s like trying to find my way out of a maze that changes its layout every time I take a step. We're the Bridge Generation, aren't we? We're building our own path but we're also just being funneled through education and society into these expectations. I recently watched an interview with Emilia Clarke and she said something about careers and plans, something that really hit home. Oh yeah, like what? She was saying that until she found what she loved doing, all she could think about was giving up because the pressure to have it all figured out was so high.

Yo, man, did you finish that history project? Nah, mate. I started it but then I got distracted and forgot about it. Oh, that sucks. You know we need good grades to make it to A levels, and then into uni, maybe? I know, I know. I mean, can’t they buy a better internet plan? Yeah, but the point is, there’s always a way out, just need to think differently, or something. Might just need to stop drinking expensive coffee. No, I don’t think it’s because they want to be, but maybe they’ve never or rarer seen an alternative. Education is a key. Totally agree. But even if they have enough education, the job market’s tough and sometimes, the system is rigged. True. I heard about this study - they followed a couple of people who were born in poorer areas for years and most of them stayed poor even if they worked as hard, sometimes harder than people from better-off areas. That’s life, innit? But it’s not fair. Exactly, and things would be easier if the government just gave the money that they spend on this or that war or excessive stuff to help people out of poverty. Right. Seems like the government's priorities are all over the place. But hey, at least we are not poor and our parents support us financially, right? Yes, that's for sure. But it’s also about what we do with what we have. True. I mean, I spend most of my cash on comics. Can’t give up that habit. LOL, truly a sacrifice for mankind. And you, anything new? Nope. Just more stuff about politics and consumerism making us all into... well, consumers rather than people. Funnily enough, that concept shows up in most of the comics I read too. The heroes are often just fighting company or government interests more than true evil. Exactly. It’s a reflection of the deeper issues in society. Yeah, and it’s weird because we read about like superpowers and all, but the real superpower is how we think and act.

So, I watched "Tenet" yesterday. Really? How was it? It was alright. I think it's one of those films that you have to watch more than once to fully understand. Aye, I agree. It's a mind-bender. Sometimes it’s just better to enjoy the ride.

So okay so I'm going to show you how to cook rice. It's pretty easy. You don't really need anything too special. Ah, that's great, thanks! You want to cover it up by about an inch. Ah, okay. And then you just bring it all to a boil? Exactly, and then you turn it down to a simmer. But you also need to check it in a bit, maybe around 10 or 15 minutes in. It should be soft but still a bit firm, you know? For a curry this is it. So nothing else goes in it at this stage? Right. You’re just cooking the rice while the curry cooks. If the curry’s a bit spicy, sometimes I also add a bit of salt while it’s cooking, but that’s it – just plain rice to soak up all that tasty curry. And in terms of seasoning for the curry? Salt, fats, and all that? Well, for the curry… it really depends on the ingredients and recipe, but usually, you're looking at finding the right balance. Some people don’t add extra salt because there’s already a lot in curry pastes, for example. But a bit of fat – like oil or butter – can help bring out the flavors. I remember one of the biggest challenges in my design work was trying to create public spaces that could bring together various groups safely and respectfully, especially in urban areas with their own social tensions.
